group.title: Travel and health
sources: Words and CEFR levels chosen by the authors from general knowledge of English; meanings, examples and sentences are original

Word-list licences checked 2026-10-25: CEFR-J Wordlist 1.5 (Tono Laboratory, TUFS; free with citation, A1-B2) and NGSL/NAWL (CC BY-SA 4.0) were not copied; Oxford 3000 and English Vocabulary Profile terms were not confirmed, so they were not used

words.meaning: An official document that you show when you travel to another country.
examples: Don’t forget your {passport} at the airport.
wrong: A passport is a small bag that you eat from.

words.meaning: The bags and cases that you take on a journey.
examples: Our {luggage} was heavy, so we took a taxi.
wrong: Luggage is a kind of fast train.

words.meaning: The act of traveling from one place to another.
examples: The {journey} from Rome to Paris takes two hours by plane.
wrong: A journey is a room where you keep clothes.

words.meaning: A journey in a plane.
examples: Our {flight} to Lima leaves at noon.
wrong: A flight is a ride on a bicycle through a forest.

words.meaning: An arrangement to keep a table, room or seat for you.
examples: I made a {reservation} for two at eight o’clock.
wrong: A reservation is a bill that you pay after dinner.

words.meaning: A person who travels in a vehicle but does not drive it.
examples: Every {passenger} must wear a seat belt.
wrong: A passenger is the person who drives the bus.

words.meaning: A person who visits a place for fun.
examples: Many {tourists} visit the old castle in summer.
wrong: A tourist is a person who lives in the same house all year.

words.meaning: The place at a station where you get on a train.
examples: The train to Leeds leaves from {platform} four.
wrong: A platform is a place in a bank where you keep money.

words.meaning: The way you take to get from one place to another.
examples: We took the shortest {route} to the beach.
wrong: A route is a kind of fruit.

words.meaning: Something you buy to remember a place you visited.
examples: I bought a small {souvenir} in Venice.
wrong: A souvenir is something you throw away at the airport.

words.meaning: The line between two countries.
examples: We showed our passports at the {border}.
wrong: A border is a kind of bed.

words.meaning: The place at an airport where officials check what you bring into a country.
examples: We had to wait a long time at {customs}.
wrong: Customs is the shop where you buy cheap food at an airport.

words.meaning: The place where someone is going.
examples: Our final {destination} is Tokyo.
wrong: A destination is the place where a trip begins.

words.meaning: The time when someone or something leaves a place.
examples: The {departure} of the bus is at six.
wrong: A departure is the time when a plane lands.

words.meaning: The time when someone or something reaches a place.
examples: The {arrival} of our train was late.
wrong: An arrival is the time when you leave home.

words.meaning: A pain in your head.
examples: I have a bad {headache} today.
wrong: A headache is a pain in your foot.

words.meaning: Something you take to get well when you are ill.
examples: Take this {medicine} twice a day.
wrong: Medicine is a kind of cold drink you buy at a movie theater.

words.meaning: A high body temperature when you are ill.
examples: The child has a {fever} and needs to rest.
wrong: A fever is the feeling of being very cold with a low temperature.

words.meaning: A sudden noise you make when air comes out of your throat.
examples: I have a bad {cough} and a sore throat.
wrong: A cough is a kind of soup.

words.meaning: A shop where you can buy medicine.
examples: I bought some tablets at the {pharmacy}.
wrong: A pharmacy is a shop that sells only clothes.

words.meaning: A vehicle that takes sick or hurt people to hospital.
examples: Someone called an {ambulance} after the accident.
wrong: An ambulance is a vehicle that carries luggage to the airport.

words.meaning: Harm to a part of your body.
examples: He had an {injury} to his knee.
wrong: An injury is a feeling of great joy.

words.meaning: In good condition; not ill.
examples: Fruit and vegetables keep you {healthy}.
wrong: Eating only sweets every day is a healthy way to live.

words.meaning: Physical activity that keeps your body strong.
examples: Walking is good {exercise}.
wrong: Exercise is the act of sitting still all day.

words.meaning: A person who looks after your teeth.
examples: I have an appointment with the {dentist} on Monday.
wrong: A dentist is a doctor who treats only your eyes.

words.meaning: A reaction of the body to something that does not bother most people.
examples: She has an {allergy} to nuts.
wrong: An allergy is a kind of exercise.

words.meaning: A bad feeling in your body when you are hurt.
examples: I felt a sharp {pain} in my back.
wrong: Pain is the feeling you have when you are very happy.

words.meaning: A piece of cloth you put around an injury.
examples: The nurse put a {bandage} on my finger.
wrong: A bandage is a kind of food.

words.meaning: To become well again after being ill.
examples: It took two weeks to {recover} from the flu.
wrong: You recover when you become more ill.

words.meaning: How hot or cold something is.
examples: The doctor checked my {temperature}.
wrong: Temperature is the sound that a clock makes.

words.meaning: A person who takes care of sick people in a hospital.
examples: The {nurse} gave me my medicine.
wrong: A nurse is a person who teaches children at school.

words.meaning: A person who is getting treatment from a doctor.
examples: The doctor saw ten {patients} this morning.
wrong: A patient is someone who treats other people in a hospital.

words.meaning: The part of your body where food goes after you eat.
examples: My {stomach} hurts after lunch.
wrong: The stomach is the part of the body that you use to see.

words.meaning: Feeling that everything is moving around you.
examples: I felt {dizzy} after I stood up quickly.
wrong: I felt dizzy because I sat quietly and was feeling perfect.

words.meaning: A large bag with a handle for carrying clothes on a journey.
examples: She packed her {suitcase} the night before.
wrong: A suitcase is a kind of cake.

words.meaning: A car with a driver that you pay to take you somewhere.
examples: We took a {taxi} to the hotel.
wrong: A taxi is a bus that always takes thirty people.

words.meaning: A boat that carries people and cars across water.
examples: The {ferry} crosses the bay every hour.
wrong: A ferry is a kind of plane.

words.meaning: Not well; sick.
examples: I stayed home because I was {ill}.
wrong: He was ill, so he ran a marathon and felt great.

words.meaning: Not strong.
examples: After the flu, I felt {weak} for a week.
wrong: He lifted a heavy box easily because he was very weak.

words.meaning: To stop work or activity and relax.
examples: You should {rest} when you are tired.
wrong: You rest when you run fast without a break.
